LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 11.3.1 INTERROGATIVES

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.3: Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Interrogatives

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Interrogatives. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: when clauses with present tense to show the future, for example, ‘When are you going to school?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify interrogatives in print or digital texts
2. use interrogatives correctly to express different meanings

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. identify interrogatives in print or digital texts
   In simple words: practise until you can identify interrogatives in print or digital texts. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

2. use interrogatives correctly to express different meanings
   In simple words: practise until you can use interrogatives correctly to express different meanings. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Interrogatives using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Interrogatives in the examples.
2. Explain Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Interrogatives to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Interrogatives.
4. Show that you can: identify interrogatives in print or digital texts

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Interrogatives using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Interrogatives important for a Grade 6 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Discuss in pairs or groups which among the following words are not interrogatives: whip, how, what, when, whom, why, which, whisper, where and whole,
2. Practise using when clauses with present tense to show the future, for example, ‘When are you going to school?
3. Create lists of interrogative sentences using words related to the theme,

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. when clauses with present tense to show the future, for example, ‘When are you going to school?
2. How do you form questions?
3. Why do we ask questions?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify interrogatives in print or digital texts
2. use interrogatives correctly to express different meanings

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
